observations.ownCompletePageObservation: The disposal/recycling item is in the common electrochemical-source content box, above the separate elevated-level additions. Both batteries and rechargeable accumulators are named. The lower BNE box supplies environmental and social consequences and the possibility of a reasoned evaluation. Nothing in the selected item demands electrode equations, recycling-plant operation or plastics chemistry.
observations.operatorFinding: The selected bullet names content without a literal assessment verb. A discussion and environmental judgment are defensible competency operationalizations in this page context; they must not be presented as a quotation from that bullet.

observations.ownCompletePageObservation: The environmental discussion appears in the right-hand column next to secondary electrochemical sources. The immediately preceding paragraph about charge/discharge processes is separate. The discussion sentence has three objects: disposal problems, extraction with an explicit rare-metal qualifier, and recycling. Its secondary-source placement prevents a primary-cell-only reading.
observations.operatorFinding: The instruction explicitly calls for discussion. The battery target includes that discussion, while the second target makes the rare-metal extraction discussion assessable on its own. The stronger environmental assessment in the battery target is acceptable as a supported operationalization, not a reason to label the individual MV edge exact.

Discuss extraction of rare metals in the electrochemical-source context
Discuss recycling in the same source context

observations.ownCompletePageObservation: The first assessment bullet on actual page 24 joins a description of recycling significance to a personal decision. Resource conservation and energy saving must both inform the judgment. Metal-production procedures and oxide reactions are other bullets, so they cannot be inserted as requirements of this one.
observations.operatorFinding: Description is an evidential basis for assessment here, not a second unrelated product. The proposed bilingual wording retains the causal link and both consumption and disposal. It does not require a quantitative life-cycle calculation.
fullSelectedDuty: Describe significance of metal recycling for conserving resources
Describe significance of metal recycling for saving energy
Use those reasons to assess personal consumption and disposal choices
